Conditional effects individuals: individuals simulated belonging different conditional cohorts (e.g. different treatment groups groups different disease statuses). Key (-key data.frame): Provide data.frame object including information genes want simulate. minimum, object must include columns specifying geneID, chromosome, location (geneMiddle). just columns, splatPop function GFF provided. Finally, provide conditional effect information (eQTL.condition, ConditionDE.ConditionN), splatPop use conditional effects instead randomly assigning . Randomly (-gff NULL -key NULL): option call mockGFF generate random GFF file specified chromosome. default option neither gff key provided. Note splatPop assign eSNPs genes within defined window, thus provided genotype gene information needs span genomic regions.

title: Introduction to Splatter
text: One thing might like simulating data compare real dataset, compare simulations different parameters models. Splatter provides function compareSCEs aims make comparisons easier. name suggests function takes list SingleCellExperiment objects, combines datasets produces plots comparing . Let’s make two small simulations see compare. returned list three items. first two combined datasets gene (RowData) cell (ColData) third contains comparison plots (produced using ggplot2), example plot distribution means:  plots might want consider easy make using returned data. example, plot number expressed genes library size:
code: sim1 <- splatSimulate(nGenes = 1000, batchCells = 20, verbose = FALSE) sim2 <- simpleSimulate(nGenes = 1000, nCells = 20, verbose = FALSE) comparison <- compareSCEs(list(Splat = sim1, Simple = sim2))  names(comparison) #> [1] "RowData" "ColData" "Plots" names(comparison$Plots) #> [1] "Means"        "Variances"    "MeanVar"      "LibrarySizes" "ZerosGene"    #> [6] "ZerosCell"    "MeanZeros"    "VarGeneCor" comparison$Plots$Means library("ggplot2") ggplot(comparison$ColData, aes(x = sum, y = detected, colour = Dataset)) +     geom_point()
